title: Temple of Vesta
visualBrief: Present-day roofless Temple of Vesta in the Roman Forum: circular exposed-brick podium, three tall fluted Corinthian columns and one mapped stump, northwest curved marble cella/entablature sector, and individually mapped low ruin fragments. The missing roof and remaining historic colonnade are not reconstructed. Independent Forum ruins remain native.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q753791/relation1842062 identifies the Roman Forum ruin. Eight current PMTiles component footprints include three full column positions, one stump, the northwest surviving sector and three low masonry fragments. Their raw east/south coordinates control placement. Ordinary northwest and reverse photographs confirm the surviving marble sector faces northwest; the old minimum-area rectangle axis is not a facade direction. In the northwest ordinary photographs the low stump appears left of the three tall columns. The northeastern end of the mapped four-column group,35184503447738, therefore remains the short stump;35184503447720/35184503447713/35184503447731 retain full height. The cella wall stops inside the western bay so the westernmost tall column stands open beneath the broken entablature. PMTiles provides positions, not these surviving heights; the signed survival assignment is picture-guided.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Ordinary photographs guide approximate podium2.05m, shaft/capital and10.35m entablature top above the occupied foundation. The ordinary article describes an approximately15m historic podium,20 original columns,6.19m architrave radius and8.6m inner cella diameter. These are plan context, not a full reconstruction or surveyed current dimensions. The outer occupied foundation is14.9m across; mapped column positions remain unchanged. Fragments, profiles, flutes and capitals are medium-fi approximations.
